Simulate a two-phase (oil-water) stratified flow in a horizontal circular pipe using the OpenFOAM solver `twoPhaseEulerFoam`. The pipe has an inner diameter of 0.1 m and a length of 2.0 m (L/D = 20), oriented along the global X-axis. Gravity acts in the negative Z-direction (perpendicular to the pipe axis) to drive oil-water stratification.
Define two phases: water (density 998 kg/m3, dynamic viscosity 0.001 Pa.s) and oil (density 850 kg/m3, dynamic viscosity 0.02 Pa.s). Use water as the primary phase.
Use the standard OpenFOAM two-phase k-epsilon mixture turbulence model (`mixtureKEpsilon` or equivalent) with the turbulent dispersion model enabled for interfacial transport of the volume fraction.
At the inlet (X = 0), impose a fixed uniform velocity boundary condition of (1.0 0 0) m/s using `type fixedValue`, and a fixed water volume fraction `alpha.water = uniform 0.3` using `type fixedValue`. Set inlet pressure to `zeroGradient`.
At the pipe walls, impose `noSlip` for both phases (velocity = 0) and `zeroGradient` for `alpha.water` (no phase flux through the wall).
At the outlet (X = 2.0 m), set `alpha.water` to `type zeroGradient`, velocity to `type zeroGradient` (or `inletOutlet`), and pressure to `type fixedValue uniform 0`.
Configure the transient solver for a steady-state convergence workflow: set `adjustTimeStep yes` and limit the Courant number to below 0.5. Set `maxDeltaT` to a value consistent with Co < 0.5. Choose an end time long enough to allow the stratified profile to fully develop (on the order of 10–50 flow-through times).
Monitor convergence by placing at least three probe locations along the pipe axis (e.g., X = 0.5, 1.0, 1.5 m) and tracking the cross-sectional average of `alpha.water`, the axial velocity magnitude, and the k and epsilon fields. Declare the simulation converged when these quantities change by less than a relative tolerance (e.g., 0.1%) over 50 consecutive time steps, then stop the run.
Generate a structured mesh with sufficient radial resolution (at least 20–30 cells across the diameter) to resolve the stratified interface, and adequate axial resolution (at least 100–200 cells over the 2 m length). The mesh must be axisymmetric or hex-dominant in cross-section to minimize numerical diffusion of the interface.
After the run reaches convergence, extract the fully-developed cross-sectional profiles of `alpha.water` and velocity at a station near the outlet (e.g., X = 1.8 m) and confirm the water fraction is concentrated along the bottom of the pipe with oil on top, consistent with a stratified flow regime.
